trends.what: A curated, searchable list of free public APIs for developers to use in their projects.
trends.why: It's the go-to resource for developers looking to quickly integrate third-party data or services, and its massive star count reflects its enduring utility.

trends.what: An open-source platform offering free, self-paced coding lessons, projects, and certifications in web development, data science, and more.
trends.why: It remains a top destination for self-learners and career-changers, and its continuous updates keep it relevant in the ever-changing tech landscape.

trends.what: A massive, community-maintained collection of free programming books, tutorials, and learning resources in multiple languages.
trends.why: It's a one-stop shop for free, high-quality learning materials, making it a perennial favorite for budget-conscious learners and educators.

trends.what: A personal AI assistant that runs locally on any OS and platform, designed to be your own private, customizable helper.
trends.why: It taps into the growing demand for local, privacy-first AI assistants that don't rely on cloud services, and its playful 'lobster way' branding adds charm.

trends.what: Interactive, visual roadmaps and guides that outline the skills and technologies needed for various developer career paths.
trends.why: It helps developers navigate the overwhelming amount of tech choices, and its interactive format makes career planning more engaging and clear.

trends.what: A tool that makes AI agents generate code with a 'lazy senior dev' mindset, prioritizing minimal, simple solutions over over-engineered ones.
trends.why: It addresses the common problem of AI generating overly complex code, and its humorous take on 'laziness' resonates with developers who value simplicity.

trends.what: A fullscreen, mouse-interactive terminal UI (TUI) harness for running coding agents, designed for extensibility and hands-on control.
trends.why: It offers a more immersive and interactive alternative to typical CLI-based coding agents, appealing to developers who want a richer terminal experience.

trends.what: A pure-C, zero-dependency runtime that runs large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) AI models on consumer hardware by streaming experts from disk.
trends.why: It democratizes access to frontier AI models by making them runnable on existing hardware, avoiding the need for expensive GPUs or cloud services.
